uñcha: [Uchi+a] (pu,thī) CL=7 (1) Anything gathered for sustenance. The practice of seeking. Seeks alms. (2) The place where seeks (such as alms). Uñcha(ti) [uñcha+a]  That should be accepted by seeks alms.
uñchācariyā: [Uñcha+cariyā] (thī) CL=7 The practice of seeking alms or wandering to obtain something from various places.
uñchācāra: [Uñchā+ācāra] (pu) CL=7 The practice of seeking alms or wandering to obtain something from various places.
uñchācārika: [Uñchācāra+ika] (ti) CL=7 A hermit who has a livelihood habit that is seeking (the requisites such as sesame, rice). See also - Uñchācariya.
uñchāsaka: [Uñchā+saka] (ti) CL=7 Involving eating by means of gleaning or begging.
uñchāya: [Uchi+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having sought. Having anything gathered for sustenance.
uññātabba: [(1)ava+ñā+tabba.(2)u+ñā+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Regarded with contempt. Disrespected. Should be looked down (on).
uññāti: [Ava+ñā+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He regards someone with contempt. He treats someone with disrespect.
